$$
{(\frac{8}{7}-\frac{1}{16})}^{0}=1.

$$
{(\frac{1}{2})}^{-3}={(\frac{2}{1})}^{3}={2}^{3}=8.

                    Evaluating Expressions With Negative Exponents
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS.

First, we compute the expression inside the parentheses:

$$
\dfrac{4}{3} \times ({\color{red}-5} + {\color{red}3})^{-2} + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3} \times ({\color{red}-2})^{-2} + \dfrac{2}{3}
$$

Next, notice that $(-2)^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{(-2)^2} = \dfrac{1}{4}.$ So, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}\times (-2)^{-2}+\frac{2}{3} & = \\ \frac{4}{3}\times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{2}{3} & = \\ \frac{4\times 1}{3\times 4}+\frac{2}{3} & = \\ \frac{\cancel{4}\times 1}{3\times \cancel{4}}+\frac{2}{3} & = \\ \frac{1}{3}+\frac{2}{3} & = \\ 1\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS.

Any number raised to the power of $0$ equals $1.$ So, we have 

$$
\left( 1.5 + \dfrac{2}{15} \right) ^0 = 1.
$$

Next, we evaluate the negative exponent and get

$$
\left(-4\right)^{-2}  = \dfrac{1}{(-4)^2} = \dfrac{1}{16}.
$$

Substituting all these values into the expression, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}2+{(-4)}^{-2}÷{(1.5+\frac{2}{15})}^{0} & = \\ 2+\frac{1}{16}÷1 & = \\ 2+\frac{1}{16} & = \\ \frac{32}{16}+\frac{1}{16} & = \\ \frac{33}{16}\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
As we know already, to evaluate numerical expressions with a mix of different operations, we follow the order of operations (PEMDAS).

The same rules apply to numerical expressions with zero and negative exponents. To demonstrate, let's compute the value of

$$
(-3)^0 +2^2 \div 2.
$$

To evaluate the given expression, we use PEMDAS.

Notice that $\left(-3\right)^{0}=1.$ So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(-3)}^{0}+{2}^{2}÷2 & = \\ 1+{2}^{2}÷2 & = \\ 1+4÷2 & = \\ 1+2 & = \\ 3 & .\end{aligned}
$$
